extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: The first Visual Question Answering (VQA) dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case, sourced from online question answering community forums (Stack Exchange). It contains 64,696 VQAs with authentic context, answers validated by the question asker, and user-chosen topics.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari
extraction.publisher: University of Texas at Austin, Microsoft, University of Colorado Boulder
extraction.citeAs: Chen, C., Liu, M., Codella, N., Li, Y., Yuan, L., & Gurari, D. (2024). Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by scraping data from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange. The raw data spanned from August 2010 to November 2022. Data collection involved extracting examples containing a natural language question (title), context (body), image (URL), and at least one answer. The dataset was filtered to include only visual questions with an accepted answer, a score greater than 0, and a single image without visual answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Publicly-available data from the Stack Exchange archive hosted at https://archive.org/details/stackexchange in XML format.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset underwent two filtering steps. First, low-quality VQAs were removed based on Stack Exchange's up-vote/down-vote system (removing questions or answers with scores 0 or less). Second, visual questions with multiple images (e.g., GIFs) or visual answers were excluded. Finally, examples where the image could not be downloaded were removed, and all images were converted to PNG format for consistency.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was split into training (665 examples), validation (285 examples), and test (63,746 examples) sets. Training and validation splits were created by randomly selecting 7 and 3 examples respectively from each of the 105 topics for topics with at least 20 examples. No topics were excluded from the test dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: User intentions were annotated by hiring three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. Workers were located in the US, had completed >500 HITs with >95% approval, and underwent one-on-one Zoom training and a qualifying test. Two independent workers annotated 105 randomly selected VQAs (one from each topic). If annotations did not match, a third worker was hired to break the tie. The final label used the majority vote from three crowdsourced labels per visual question. Additionally, domain experts (10 annotators with Master's degrees or higher in specific fields) rated model-generated answers as correct, partially correct, or incorrect for a subset of 200 VQAs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (for user intention annotation); Home-grown web-based interface (for domain expert evaluation).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For user intention annotation, agreement accuracy improved from 53.3% to 87.5% and Cohen's kappa improved from 45.24% to 84.69% over four rounds of annotator analysis. For domain expert evaluation, inter-annotator agreement was not explicitly quantified, but experts were compensated and trained to ensure quality.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (for user intention labels on the subset); 1 (for domain expert ratings on the evaluation subset).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers: Located in the United States, >500 HITs completed, >95% approval rating. Domain Experts: Located in the United States, at least a Master's degree in a field related to their assigned VQA topic (e.g., Physical Fitness, Botany, Music, Mechanics, Politics, Law, Chinese Language, Economics, Statistics, Artificial Intelligence).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5 was used to bootstrap initial user intention categories via zero-shot prompting.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to facilitate the research community's continued improvement of VQA models for authentic use cases. It may benefit real-world applications such as community question answering platforms, learning assistance tools, virtual assistants, and visual search. However, the dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas due to the digital divide, and geographic representation is unbalanced (more from US, India, Europe; less from Egypt).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset reflects the biases of Stack Exchange users, who have access to mobile devices and the Internet. Geographic representation is unbalanced, with more data from the US, India, and Europe compared to countries like Egypt. The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas. Models trained on or evaluated with this data may exhibit biases related to language (performing better on Germanic/Romance languages than East Asian or Cyrillic scripts) and topic (performing better on Science than Culture & Recreation).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas. Geographic representation is unbalanced. The answers are considerably longer (mean 173 words) than typical VQA datasets, making standard VQA evaluation metrics ineffective. The dataset is limited to English-language questions primarily, though multilingual VQAs are included. The domain expert evaluation was limited to 10 topics and 200 VQAs, which may not fully represent the entire dataset's difficulty level.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning of Visual Question Answering models. Specifically designed for evaluating long-form text generation and authentic use case generalization.
